propositions: Mirror Guard primary watcher (GitHub Actions workflow) fails on single instantaneous SHA sample during expected post-submit replication lag, despite the module's design delegating lag absorption to the alarm layer (proven in docstring and CloudWatch secondary with sustained-divergence window).

The workflow's run() fetches once and maps diverged sample to exit 1, but replication_verdict's own design contract requires the alarm layer to implement a sustained-divergence evaluation window to absorb transient ~15s post-submit lag.
Incomplete-implementation defect caused by a774's commit d96628c9dca: the designed lag-absorption window was documented in the module but never wired into the workflow surface.

In-process persistence wrapper with configurable re-sampling (3 attempts, 45s spacing by default, ~6x documented lag) returns healthy on convergence and unhealthy only when divergence persists across the window.
Non-converged outcomes (static GitHub tip, moving never-converging tip) still fail exit 1 with reason and sample count; GitHub-ahead/foreign divergence never converges so it remains loud every run.
Fixes red runs on self-healing lag (run 32567576681 +16min pattern) while keeping true outages and replication stalls loud; no CI-provider-specific state — portable in-module implementation.
